💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 19:40.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has officially begun his Manchester United reign, but his first press conferences at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States offer a revealing insight into how he intends to tackle the crisis at Old Trafford.
  • The Argentine arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, November 18, having completed his final international assignment with the United States, and faces an immediate challenge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 18 Nov 2026 19:40.

Mauricio Pochettino has officially begun his Manchester United reign, but his first press conferences at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States offer a revealing insight into how he intends to tackle the crisis at Old Trafford.

The Argentine arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, November 18, having completed his final international assignment with the United States, and faces an immediate challenge against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

United sit 18th in the Premier League after winning just one of their opening 10 matches, with Michael Carrick's dismissal leaving Pochettino responsible for restoring confidence to a squad struggling for results.

The 54-year-old has inherited troubled teams before, although few appointments have offered such little preparation time before a fixture of this magnitude.

Looking back at his opening statements in four previous jobs reveals a recurring approach: Pochettino tends to publicly back the players he inherits, avoid making immediate transfer demands and emphasise the importance of collective responsibility.

Those principles have helped him transform some teams, but his experiences at PSG and Chelsea also demonstrate that they do not guarantee success.

When Pochettino arrived at Tottenham in 2014, the club were searching for stability after a disappointing campaign under Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood.

The Argentine had built his reputation at Southampton, where his energetic pressing system and ability to develop young players attracted considerable attention.

At his first major press engagement with Spurs, he resisted suggestions that widespread recruitment was necessary.

"We have an unbelievable squad with unbelievable players," Pochettino insisted.

"The most crucial thing is to develop our players and to provide the best team to play on the pitch.".

His message was clear: improving the existing squad would take priority over demanding upcoming signings.

That approach eventually helped Tottenham establish themselves among the Premier League's leading clubs.

Pochettino guided Spurs to second place in 2016-17 and reached the Champions League final in 2019, although he departed later that year without winning a trophy.

His appointment at PSG in January 2021 presented a different challenge.

Rather than developing a relatively young Premier League squad, Pochettino inherited a team containing established superstars, including Neymar and Kylian Mbappe.

During his introductory press conference, the Argentine again rejected the idea of imposing a rigid tactical system regardless of the available personnel.

Discussing the roles of Neymar and Mbappe, he explained that his responsibility was to find positions in which they could express their abilities and become decisive.

He also emphasised that a team's behaviour with and without possession mattered more than the formation displayed on paper.

The flexibility he promised was tested by the demands of managing an exceptionally talented squad.

Although PSG won Ligue 1 in 2021-22, Pochettino failed to deliver the Champions League success the club wanted and departed that summer.

Chelsea offered another rebuilding assignment in 2023.

The Blues had finished 12th in the Premier League after a turbulent campaign, and Pochettino was tasked with restoring their competitiveness following extensive changes to the playing squad.

At his first press conference, he acknowledged that performances alone would not satisfy expectations at Stamford Bridge.

"My target is to win," he declared.

The Argentine also expressed confidence in the club's sporting structure, explaining that he had accepted the owners' strategic plan rather than seeking greater authority over recruitment.

His Chelsea side eventually recovered to finish sixth and reached the EFL Cup final, but an inconsistent campaign ended with his departure by mutual consent in May 2024.

The experience demonstrated the difficulty of introducing a long-term playing philosophy while facing pressure for immediate results.

Pochettino's introductory press conference with the United States in September 2024 provided perhaps the clearest indication of the demands United's players can expect.

The former Tottenham manager made collective effort central to his philosophy, insisting that individual talent would only be effective within a properly organised team.

"But when we don't have the ball, we need to run, we need to be aggressive, we need to be competitive," he explained.

He also stressed that his coaching staff needed to create an environment in which players understood their responsibilities and could express their abilities.

That message carries particular relevance at Old Trafford.

United have conceded 19 goals in their opening 10 Premier League matches and have struggled to produce the collective intensity required to compete consistently.

Pochettino's preference for coordinated pressing could offer one route towards improvement, although implementing those principles will require time and careful management of the squad's physical condition.

His previous appointments suggest that he is unlikely to begin by publicly criticising individual players or demanding a major January overhaul.

At Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea, his introductory message focused on working with the players already available, with recruitment generally left to the club's decision-makers.

That approach may be particularly crucial at United, where the relationship between the head coach and the sporting department will come under scrutiny as the January transfer window approaches.

Pochettino also has a record of improving young players, an asset for a squad featuring talents such as Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo and Benjamin Sesko.

However, the circumstances surrounding his arrival leave little opportunity for a gradual introduction.

Unlike at Chelsea, where he benefited from a full pre-season, the Argentine has only a handful of training sessions before facing Liverpool.

United's position in the relegation zone also creates a more urgent challenge than the long-term projects he initially discussed at Tottenham or with the United States.

His opening press conferences across those four jobs suggest he will seek to protect his players publicly while demanding greater effort and discipline behind the scenes.

Whether those familiar principles can produce an immediate response will become clearer at Anfield, where Pochettino faces one of the most difficult possible introductions to life as Manchester United manager.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Walking into a club in turmoil is nothing new for Mauricio Pochettino.
  • He arrived at Southampton with the Saints three points clear of the relegation zone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 14 November 2026.

Walking into a club in turmoil is nothing new for Mauricio Pochettino.

He arrived at Southampton with the Saints three points clear of the relegation zone. Tottenham Hotspur were crying out for some leadership after Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood's spells, while Chelsea picked up Pochettino in 2023 on the back of their lowest league finish for more than 25 years.

According to recent reports, now it's Manchester United that require what Victor Wanyama once described as Pochettino's 'magic touch' – and they need it quick as they sit in the relegation zone with ten games played. Pochettino remains weeks removed from the January transfer window and has a number of first-team regulars out with long-term injuries, so his reputation of improving the players at his disposal will be put to the test.

He has developed a reputation for placing faith in youth – while at Tottenham, Pochettino handed 12 debuts to players aged 21 or under, more than any other manager.

Money will be tight and United look almost certain to miss out on next season's Champions League, which will make squad development significantly harder, so Pochettino will have to make do and mend with a lot of the current underperforming crop of players.

With all that in mind, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over the 36 players Pochettino will be inheriting when he walks through the door at Carrington next week.

And you can scroll to the end of the article to have your say on who should stay, and who should go...

Mauricio Pochettino will rapidly have to assess which Man United players to discard.

It has been revealed that lammens won't be going anywhere. He is United's No 1 and despite a downturn in form this season, he's not become a bad goalkeeper overnight. Pochettino's trusted goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez will almost certainly replace Craig Mawson to bring some fresh ideas.

Industry observers note that jimenez focuses a lot on developing goalkeepers to be comfortable as sweepers and playing higher up. That is a sore spot in Lammens' game – recently exposed by Bournemouth striker Evanilson – but proper coaching should help develop Lammens, just like Jimenez developed Hugo Lloris.

Recent findings suggest that A summer arrival from Leeds United as a back-up goalkeeper. Pochettino has more key problems than messing around with his No2.

Heaton is hugely popular at the club and while he doesn't play, he is viewed as a vital cog in the dressing room given his wealth of experience. He turns 41 later this season and has been busy preparing for life away from the pitch.

Heaton has completed courses on becoming a sporting director, as well as an executive leadership short course from Oxford University.

He also holds his goalkeeper coach B-Licence, A-Licence outfield, and a certificate of football management from UEFA.

Industry observers note that pochettino would be wise to keep Heaton in-house, even if not as a player. He is a respected figure who knows United inside out and that shouldn't be overlooked as Pochettino tries to build out a culture.

Senne Lammens (right) has made a shaky start to the season but will be going nowhere.

Dalot is highly respected by every manager that works with him for the effort he puts in, something that can't always be mentioned of some of his team-mates.

But he is woefully short of the required quality to take United forward and he is not a comfortable fit for Pochettino's ideals, either.

Pochettino gets width in his sides via the full backs and that requires a relentless runner – which Dalot is – having quality both defensively and in attack, which Dalot does not.

Recent findings suggest that malo Gusto, who is keen to leave Chelsea and could become a key target for United, spoke of how Pochettino developed his game in 2024 when he noted: 'He helps us a lot. He has tried to show us the desire to win, to keep fighting against every team.

Recent findings suggest that 'He talks to us a lot about tactics, technique and everything. He is a good person as well. He tries to help us a lot on the pitch and off it. He is a good coach for this young team.

'He is here for this. He knows he has to wake up our mentality, to wake up our desire to win everything.'.

United have neglected their back-line for years and it's time for a dramatic refresh, starting with shifting Dalot, who is under contract until 2028.

It is time for Man United to move on from Diogo Dalot - he is short of the quality required.

Noussair Mazraoui (Full back, 28).

Dalot has at least shown he has the engine to get up and down, which could offer a lifeline under Pochettino, but Mazraoui hasn't.

Full backs are essential to Pochettino's high-intensity, high press 4-2-3-1, and that's not a formula that suits Mazraoui's abilities.

Privately, sources close to the dressing room have suggested in recent weeks that Mazraoui, another under contract until 2028, is keen for a upcoming challenge.

Matthijs de Ligt (centre back, 27).

Overhauling the defence is one of the main topics of conversation among agents and players right now but De Ligt's future is secure at Old Trafford.

He is under contract until 2029, with the option of a further year, and many figures behind the scenes believe he can bounce back from such a long period out with injury to be a success.

De Ligt's injury record, as well as the fact he isn't a natural fit for Pochettino's idea of the perfect, mobile centre back, makes him an intriguing prospect.

Strong in physical duels, he could become a key squad player.

Harry Maguire (centre back, 33).

Maguire has taken more criticism than most during his time at United and deserves credit for how he has overcome it.

His contract expires in the summer, with the option of a further year, and Maguire has described playing for United as the 'ultimate honour' so is unlikely to agitate to leave.

That being said, Pochettino puts a lot of emphasis on recovery pace given the high line he has favoured in the past and the Argentine's tactics have routinely exposed centre backs in transition, with speed essential to masking shortcomings.

Maguire would undoubtedly struggle in that department and while his physical profile would appeal, he said earlier this year that he does not want to be kept around for 'sentimental value'.

'I love this club. But it's got to be right for myself, it's got to be right for the club as well,' Maguire remarked in March before a one-year extension was triggered.

'I don't want to be staying on sentimental value. I want to be staying because I want to be there and the club want me to drive the club forward still, and they feel like I've got a substantial part to play in it.'.

The prospect of a diminishing role, with United planning multiple defensive reinforcements, may see both sides agree it's time for a change.

After seven years it may be time for Harry Maguire to move on, with his contract expiring.

Lisandro Martinez (centre back, 28).

A player that looks to have one foot out the door after calling out director of football Jason Wilcox following the defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Recent findings suggest that it's funny, almost, given Pochettino's arrival should suit Martinez down to the ground. In theory, he is the exact type of player his compatriot would implore his bosses to recruit.

Pochettino puts huge emphasis on passing out from the back and Martinez is the best in that category among United's centre backs.

Pochettino is also incredibly intense, something Martinez has been for some time at United, sometimes to the group's benefit and sometimes to its detriment.

The Argentine's contract expires in the summer and while there is an option to trigger a further year to avoid a World Cup winner walking away for nothing, the expectation is that he won't agree to a newly introduced one and his time at United is more likely than not drawing to a close.

He holds a desire to play in Spain and that may not vanish overnight. But if anyone can connect with Martinez about a longer-term role, it's a fellow Argentine.

VERDICT: Keep (but expect to go!).

Patrick Dorgu (Full back/winger, 22).

Has the potential to be the biggest winner of the Pochettino appointment.

Industry observers note that pochettino's full-back-turned-winger style totally plays into Dorgu's hands given both his engine and his comfort playing higher up the pitch. Look at the development of Danny Rose – who played more games for Pochettino than any other player – and Kyle Walker, as well as Sergino Dest with the USA.

Dorgu has a lot of the attributes Pochettino craves while he also remains raw enough that intense, but targeted, coaching could improve him.

He should immediately become one of Pochettino's go-to men.

Where there are concerns around Maguire's ability to play in a system which squeezes everyone that bit higher up the pitch, Yoro should thrive.

He showed against Villa, with a chase down to deny Nicolas Jackson a run on goal, that he possesses the necessary recovery pace.

Pochettino's centre backs need to be strong passers and Yoro can improve in this area, although he has shown a willingness to dictate with long diagonals, as well as burst through lines as a ball-carrier.

United need five reliable centre backs in the squad moving forward and Yoro can establish himself as the No1.

Given Pochettino's track record with young players, he should be really excited at becoming a key piece of the puzzle under him.

A reunion… but one that may not last very long.

In a 2017 book about Pochettino, Shaw revealed his desire to work under him again and that wish has now come true.

'With Southampton he achieved the impossible,' stated Shaw. 'We were one of the best footballing teams in the league... I do hope that I can play for him again one day. And I think he really wants me to play under him again.'.

Pochettino used to call Shaw his 'son' and their relationship has stayed strong over the years.

But Pochettino is also a winner and will be acutely aware that Shaw cannot maintain the levels that Pochettino will require from his full backs after years of injury problems.

Sources close to the player have suggested the potential for a one-year extension given the relationship with Pochettino, even if those same sources believe the time is right for a fresh start.

A long servant but not one that can take United forward from this lowest of ebbs.

Luke Shaw and Pochettino enjoyed success together at Southampton but the reunion won't last long.

Arriving as an Ineos project, United aren't going to cut their losses on Heaven just yet.

His strong passing ability will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches and he's worth a season of proper coaching to see how high or low his ceiling is.

Heaven can be reckless, particularly in his approach to tackling, but he's got a good physical profile and those who have worked with him have praised his approach to training and willingness to listen to coaches.

United are likely to go out and sign two fresh centre backs in the summer – at least they hope to – but Heaven should get a shot at development as a bit-part player.

Wholly ignored despite a left back crisis this season, Amass is widely expected to be out the door in January.

It is hard to blame him, either, given United's decision to keep him around has stunted his development.

Amass is a strong crosser of the ball and, in time, could develop into a full back in Pochettino's vision.

But neither Amass nor Pochettino will have time to wait and see. With a left back high on the shopping list, to go with Dorgu's expected ascension, this relationship shouldn't last too long.

An academy player to keep an eye on.

Kamason has played both at right back and right wing for United's Under 21s and that plays massively into his hands in a bid to try and catch the eye of his new manager.

The United youngster is a well-rounded full back that constantly looks to get forward, all while not neglecting his defensive responsibilities.

Kamason has trained regularly with the first team in recent months and that could be a sign of things to come under Pochettino, too.

United rolled the dice on Leon a year ago in a deal worth an initial £3.3million – but the move has not worked out at all.

The 19-year-old hasn't come close to making a first-team appearance and his agent has even suggested they are getting itchy feet despite sub-par performances for United's Under 21s.

'If there isn't a strategy to break into the first team between December and January, we'll look for a way out for him,' Leon's representative Renato Bittar admitted. 'A loan somewhere where he can compete, get playing time, and return to Manchester.'.

Having observed the academy teams closer than most in recent seasons, Leon hasn't shown anywhere near enough to merit becoming a project player for Pochettino.

Mount left for United in the same summer Pochettino was hired by Chelsea, so their crossover was minimal.

How much say Pochettino had in that decision remains unclear, perhaps it was insignificant, but now they will finally work together.

Mount feels disposable, not least because he hasn't registered a single assist in the Premier League for United since joining in 2023 for £60million.

With so many options ahead of him in those inverted winger roles, and with Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans preferred as No 10s, Mount needs shifting.

Bruno Fernandes (Midfielder, 32).

Contract talks have stalled in recent weeks and months but an ambitious latest manager could swing momentum back towards reigning Player of the Year Fernandes staying at Old Trafford.

The way Pochettino platformed Christian Eriksen and Dele Alli at Tottenham, as well as Cole Palmer at Chelsea, suggests Fernandes will get the role he needs to be at his very best.

Sources indicate that fernandes' mobility, and ability to run beyond his centre forward, is a strength, as is his vision to supply team-mates in open play and at set-pieces. If Fernandes plays well, so do United, generally. Pochettino favours inverted attackers, so Fernandes could even start off the left if his manager wanted to position Matheus Cunha or Tielemans more centrally.

'He's given me the freedom to play my stuff and I like it when he frees you because I feel I can express my stuff more,' Palmer said of Pochettino's coaching back in 2024.

'I'm loving it. Every day he's talking to you about different things, not just football things but life things as well. He's good at making you feel good and trying to get the best out of you.'.

That's music to the ears of Fernandes.

Pochettino's free-flowing approach could be exactly what is needed to keep Bruno Fernandes.

Pochettino knows all about Santos having worked with him at Chelsea when he was a teenager still finding his way.

The reports at that time, during a pre-season tour in North Carolina and Philadelphia, were that Santos' profile appealed to Pochettino, only for the club to go ahead and sanction loan moves to Nottingham Forest and then Strasbourg.

Santos is a summer arrival for £50m and will get more time to find his role in this United side.

He has enough talent to become a reliable deputy to Baleba as the deep-lying midfielder when everyone is fully fit.

Youri Tielemans (Midfielder, 29).

Tielemans is a high-IQ player that signed a five-year contract in the summer so, truthfully, won't be going anywhere.

That being mentioned, Tielemans' running power isn't there and the demands of a Pochettino system, if he is still the same coach that bowed out at Chelsea, may make that secondary midfield role difficult.

It feels like Tielemans could be a specialist player that Pochettino uses in games where his side expect to dominate possession.

Tielemans' composure on the ball is superior to that of many of his team-mates and that's not a trait Pochettino will overlook quickly, even if he reportedly had reservations on a younger Tielemans when he was managing at Tottenham.

In a recent development, A major winner. The £70m summer signing needs to be used in the correct way to realise his potential and Pochettino's track record should be music to Baleba's ears.

Pochettino has typically liked one of his central midfielders to drop deep in possession to create a back three – see Eric Dier at Tottenham – and Baleba should be comfortable fulfilling that role.

Moises Caicedo and Wanyama are two other success stories in the deeper No6 role that Baleba should now thrive in under Pochettino's watch, with his combativeness and tackling making him a natural fit.

'Tactically, he has taught me a lot,' Wanyama previously noted of Pochettino.

According to recent reports, 'Before, I was just thinking, "I'll just sit here and defend". But if you're playing for him, it's not only defending. You have to attack also. You have to know the right time. I have learned so much from him.'.

Now it's time for Baleba to study up and take his game to the next level.

Carlos Baleba has a had a slow start to life at United but a managerial change could unlock his potential.

It transpired that Pochettino wanted to make Ugarte his first signing at Chelsea, only for United to get in ahead of them for the Uruguayan.

Ugarte was all set to leave United in the summer were it not for a serious injury at the World Cup that left him sidelined for months.

Pochettino liked the profile of player he saw when Ugarte was scouted at Sporting Lisbon but he looks a different, far less effective, player in England.

Minds appear to be made up upstairs when it comes to moving on from Ugarte.

Where Baleba will need to drop deep, the other midfielder in Pochettino's system is the one who is expected to drive and bypass midfield blocks.

Pochettino will be acutely aware that Mainoo is extremely popular among United fans and while athleticism is often levelled against him as a weak point in his game, Pochettino will need to find a way of improving that while also nurturing his many talents.

Tottenham's Mousa Dembele was moulded by Pochettino from an attacking midfielder into a deep-lying controller, urged to dribble to break lines and open up the game.

Mainoo has many similar traits to others Pochettino has worked with, such as Weston McKennie with the US national team.

Recent findings suggest that 'They will get pushed in training more than the games they will be playing. It is all a mental thing,' former Southampton striker Rickie Lambert once remarked.

If Mainoo can come through the initial boot camp, he can flourish.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of United's top talents and will stay but has to improve his physicality.

A better player than people give him credit for but one that really needs to put a full season together at first-team level to see where he is at.

That won't be under Pochettino at United but United, if they really believe he can be part of their future, need to find Fletcher a loan move where he can feature in 35-40 games.

Clubs in League One would be all over him.

Tyler Fletcher (Midfielder, 19).

The deep-lying midfielder that can drop in to form a back three is fundamental to how Pochettino wants to play and that's a style that would suit Tyler Fletcher, rather than the more attacking Jack.

Again, figures at United and up in Scotland, just want to see Fletcher get a run of games under his belt.

Kilmarnock wanted him in the summer, but United wanted to keep Fletcher in house.

If Pochettino and United really care about his career, he should be one of the first out the door on loan in January.

Senior academy figures are the most excited about Thwaites' potential, even if it would be unfair to expect him to make a massive impact on the first team in the near future.

Technically his level is particularly high, a European pass-first, press-resistant game that will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches.

But physically there is a way to go, which should mean Thwaites is kept around as a project player.

Brought in as an Ineos project piece, after two mediocre loan spells in Switzerland with Lausanne, it's time to have Kone come back into the building and put him to work with a relentless coach like Pochettino.

Kone's twitchy game-style and desire to break through lines makes him something of a hybrid of players Pochettino has coached in the past.

Having watched him up close in the academy set-up before he went out on loan, and spoken to those who coached Kone then, it would be a major gamble for Pochettino to put his trust in him.

But Kone's ceiling feels sky high. It's time to see if he can go into the lab and come out as a Dembele-Wanyama hybrid.

VERDICT: Keep as project player.

Cristian Orozco (Midfielder, 18).

Physically he has an advanced profile for his age but United have long preached that they want to take things slow as Orozco settles into life in England and gets a grip of the language.

He is neat and tidy on the ball and has shown an ability to zip passes through the lines but not enough to suggest an elevation to the first-team group.

Academy football doesn't develop players quickly enough so a carefully selected loan move, perhaps in a technical league like the Netherlands or Belgium, would be ideal.

He needs to look at how Pochettino used players like Lucas Moura and Eriksen in the past to see how he can take his game to the next level.

Cunha has a swagger about him that United like and while he was better suited to Ruben Amorim's system than he was Michael Carrick's, Pochettino's preference for narrow wide players, funnelling them into central areas while full backs create the width, means this managerial shift should play into his hands.

'Cunha is a maverick who does things that are hard to find in some players,' Amorim once said of the Brazilian.

Recent findings suggest that 'He plays with the ball, but he has an aura that can do something to the opponent's heads. And that is really crucial.'.

It was recently suggested to Daily Mail Sport that a move for Rashford could be explored as early as January, with a desire to go back abroad.

A managerial change always puts things into flux and not least given that Pochettino said in 2022 that he'd 'always liked' Rashford, before adding: 'I think he's a great player. He just needs the confidence and for himself to believe, to put him at the top level. The quality is there for him.'.

Pochettino is unlikely to have changed an opinion as solid as that one in the years that followed and so it will be curious to see if Rashford could become the athletic, pressing No9 in Benjamin Sesko's absence.

Rashford wants to feel the love and has shown what he can do when his confidence is high. It isn't right now but don't bet against Pochettino showing him that love.

Rashford has been linked with another move away but could become a pressing No 9.

One of the more interesting profiles for Pochettino to consider.

On the face of it, Zirkzee lacks the intensity in the press and the mobility that Pochettino demands of his forwards.

Yet, Zirkzee can drop in, allowing the No10 to run in behind, which Pochettino values in a striker.

In the long term, expect Zirkzee to depart. In the short term, Pochettino may see him as a very specific tool to exploit certain opponents.

Tenacious defensively after improving immeasurably out of possession under Amorim, that's a big plus for Amad in the eyes of Pochettino.

He's among the glut of hybrid 10-wingers that United seem to stockpile and, once Sesko returns, Amad will find himself locked in a battle with Shea Lacey and Bryan Mbeumo for regular starts.

Amad's energy should give him the edge from day one to be a natural fit for Pochettino's high press.

Pochettino loves working with young players and Lacey is ready-made for that inverted winger style that the Argentine prefers, so he should be licking his lips at the prospect of more opportunities.

Lacey has played both off the right and as a No10 in academy teams and that stands him in good stead to operate in central areas, as well as isolate his full back one v one, which too many in this squad are not confident to do.

Lacey should be studying the development of Dele Alli under Pochettino and hoping he can bring his game on similarly.

Shea Lacey is (right) is a hugely promising youngster who will love working with Pochettino.

Like Cunha, Mbeumo looked a more natural fit in Amorim's two-10s system and there are similarities that could put him back in those positions under Pochettino.

He's played a lot as a No 9 and may need to deputise there for the time being but the long-term dilemma for Pochettino will be the battle between Mbeumo, Amad and Lacey cutting in from the right.

It's one of the few areas of the pitch where there will be decent competition for places.

Mbeumo will need to find a position and master it or he may be caught in between roles.

Injured until, most likely, the end of January and so it will take some time for Pochettino to get his teeth into Sesko's development.

The Slovenian feels very close to Pochettino's ideal No9 profile given his athleticism, physicality in the air, ability to press from the front and his instinctive finishing ability.

Benjamin Sesko could raise his level under a manager who routinely improves forwards.

Academy sources feel the teenager, who arrived for an initial £4million, has been unfairly criticised so far as he tries to adapt to a new club since moving up from Tottenham.

Thompson has picked up in recent academy games but in terms of his profile he looks more comfortable as a touchline winger, minus the blistering pace we usually see in that position.

His best bet is to remain in the academy and look towards a season-long loan next season.

One of the most intriguing academy prospects now that JJ Gabriel is closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

Ajayi looks physically capable of holding his own in first-team sessions and before a ball was kicked this term the development proposal was to have him make a first-team debut before the season was out.

On-pitch failings may kick that can down the road but Ajayi is comfortable anywhere across the front line, has an acceleration that's invaluable and a technical level beyond his years.

Pochettino needs to take him under his wing to see what he can squeeze out of him before next summer.

VERDICT: Integrate into first-team training.

New Phil Neumann enhancement has Birmingham City fan 'massively relieved'

  • Birmingham have scored three or more goals in four of their last six matches whilst also conceding the fewest number of goals in the Championship thus far - 14.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City's league-leading start to the Championship season has been the culmination of many key factors, none more so than the consistency displayed by Chris Davies' side.

A 10th-placed finish last term gave the Blues boss plenty of foundations to build from, even if the season as a whole was one of mixed fortunes in terms of both results and performance levels.

Birmingham have scored three or more goals in four of their last six matches whilst also conceding the fewest number of goals in the Championship thus far - 14.

Those within Davies' rearguard have earned plenty of praise for their contributions towards such exploits, but in the case of German centre-back Phil Neumann, it has also led to exit talk.

Neumann, 29, has been an ever-present alongside Birmingham captain, Christoph Klarer, so far this season, following on from an intriguing first campaign in English football after leaving Hannover 96.

The German youth international had previously been the subject of interest from clubs such as Sassuolo, Hull City and Borussia Mönchengladbach, but recent reports have suggested that Nottingham Forest, Fiorentina, Coventry City, Ipswich Town and the Tigers are plotting a potential January move for the towering figure.

Given the nature of modern football, Neumann has since revealed that he is aware of such speculation, but, to the delight of Blues fans, stated that his main aim is to return his current employers to the Premier League.

Sources indicate that "Of course I hear about those kinds of reports, but I don't pay much attention to them. I have my advisors for that, people I trust who handle those matters," he told Transfermarkt.

It has been revealed that "My full focus is on Birmingham City and what we've set out to achieve as a team. There's nothing more crucial to me than doing everything I can to achieve our goals with the club.

Sources indicate that "We have a big task ahead of us, and that's where I'm concentrating all my energy. Everything else is secondary at the moment.".

Neumann's total of 12.1 defensive contributions per 90 is right now the seventh-highest figure of any Championship player and the largest amongst Birmingham's squad at present, which comes on top of his brace against Wrexham in August that sealed the first of eight victories so far for Davies' side.

Such metrics only back up the defender's commitment to the promotion cause at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park, and Football League World's Birmingham City fan pundit, Jason Moore, is one of many supporters who have been reassured by Neumann's words.

"Massively relieved," Moore told FLW.

"I sort of expected him to have that mindset because his family's settled here, he's settled here, he's performing really well.

"I get the interest because he's performing well. But, I expected that he'd just knuckle down and focus on the club. It's a massive relief.

Blues fans, what did you make of Phil Neumann's comments? Tell us below!

"He's been an absolute rock. I honestly believe we've got the best centre-back partnership in the league. I don't think there's many that come close to potentially touching either of them," he added.

It has been revealed that "To have him focused and just wanting to keep performing for the club and wanting to go for promotion is just a massive relief. Touchwood, he stays focused, and we can achieve great stuff this season.".

Neumann may have never played top-flight football in his career so far, but with the defender in his prime years, he is very much on the cusp of earning those stripes in one form or another.

Given Birmingham's lofty short and long-term ambitions, it is no surprise that the defender wants to aid those plans whilst continuing to be valued as a first-team regular, which wouldn't necessarily be guaranteed if a January move was sanctioned.

Moore recently told FLW that the Second City outfit should only consider offers if they were between the £15m and £20m ballpark, but if Neumann continues his remarkable partnership with Klarer over the next 31 matches, there is every chance Tom Wagner could land over 10 times' as much cash.

  • Nottingham Forest target Gabriel Morais Silva Bontempo is not yet ready for the Premier League, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 18 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 18 Nov 2026 20:30.

Nottingham Forest target Gabriel Morais Silva Bontempo is not yet ready for the Premier League, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

It has been revealed that the Santos midfielder has reportedly been tracked by Forest for much of 2026, with Oliver Glasner's side weighing up a move in the January transfer window. Bournemouth are also said to be interested.

Bontempo, who turns 22 in January, has enjoyed a breakthrough year, contributing six goals and five assists in 50 appearances, and he earned his first Brazil call-up in September.

The lynchpin's contract runs until 2030, though, and speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery expressed doubts over whether the youngster could handle the step up to English football.

Sources indicate that "He's had to grow up very quickly as a central midfielder with Santos," Vickery said. "His first year was a prolonged battle against relegation, and it is a team full of veterans, which puts a lot of strain on a young midfielder.

According to recent reports, "He really has to cover the ground and link the play. He's a good little give-and-go midfielder.

According to recent reports, "Premier League, now I have my doubts. He's around the six-foot mark, so he's not small, but he is physically quite flimsy.

Recent findings suggest that "Everyone who comes from South American football to the Premier League says the same thing: 'You've got to play quicker. You must know what you're going to do with the ball before it comes.'.

Sources indicate that "In a Premier League midfield, I think he could be eaten up. I wouldn't see him as a player who's Premier League ready at the moment.".

Rather than Bontempo, Vickery believes Forest should consider a familiar face in Danilo.

The 25-year-old broke his ankle on the opening day of the 2024-25 season against Bournemouth, and he joined Botafogo the following summer in a club-record deal worth around €22m (£19.2m).

Danilo was in superb form during the first half of 2026 and earned a place in Brazil's World Cup squad, but his hopes of securing a move to a Premier League side playing in the Champions League have yet to materialise.

"Forest could do a lot worse than get the left-footed, strong, quick-thinking, versatile Danilo back," Vickery added.

"At the moment, he's a better bet than Gabriel Bontempo, who is certainly one for the long term rather than now.".

Danilo scored six goals and set up four more in 10 appearances for Nottingham Forest and was also linked with Manchester United during the summer transfer window.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the next month or so, a fair portion of the population with a love of football will be intrigued to see how Wayne Rooney fares on ITV hit show, I'm A Celebrity, Get Me Out of Here.

The 41-year-old is one of the most iconic strikers ever produced in English football, having skyrocketed to fame with his iconic goal for Everton against Arsenal in 2002.

In his playing days, Rooney became Manchester United's all-time leading scorer whilst winning several trophies and individual accolades, and after a brief return to Merseyside, found himself donning the colours of Derby County in the Championship.

The former forward then earned praise for his managerial spell at Pride Park as a youthful Rams side competed valiantly in the face of adversity, and would have survived were it not for a 21-point deduction.

The less said about Rooney's dugout spells at Birmingham City and Plymouth Argyle, the better, but during the three spells, he would have learned plenty about what it takes to succeed in one of European football's toughest divisions.

However, a claim made earlier in 2026 by the former England great is certainly looking pear-shaped at this moment in time.

Following his dismissal at Home Park in December 2024, Rooney is yet to return to management but has become a regular fixture on our TV screens with Amazon Prime, as well as his analysis on Match of the Day.

He is also a regular pundit on The Overlap with Sky Sports duo, Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher, where major talking points are discussed and analysed at length, as well as being in conversation with supporters.

Earlier this year, it was put to Rooney by Carragher as to what his 'ideal' Premier League would look like, and in doing so, the former pinpointed three clubs he would like to see make the 'significant time in the coming years'.

Two of those were Wrexham and Preston North End, who both reside in the Championship right now, with the Red Dragons certainly one of the EFL's most ambitious clubs under Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac's ownership, while North End are one of the country's most historic clubs, but have not played top-level football for 65 years.

The North Wales outfit's story has gained plenty of traction, as their Hollywood owners have invested heavily in various aspects of the club, particularly on the pitch.

With Phil Parkinson at the helm, Wrexham achieved an unprecedented three successive promotions from the National League to the Championship, before adding further depth and quality last season with the likes of Callum Doyle, Issa Kabore, Lewis O'Brien, Nathan Broadhead, Kieffer Moore and Josh Windass.

Although the club have certainly spent more than the sums of cash coming into the Racecourse Ground in player sales, the strategy very nearly worked for a fourth-straight season, but a slow start saw Parkinson's side narrowly miss out on a play-off spot.

However, there haven't been many indications that promotion will be achieved this season due to an inconsistent start, in which experienced players such as Broadhead and Windass have suffered injury misfortune, as they sit 15th in the table despite a return of four points from six against high-flying Middlesbrough and Wolves before the international break.

Circumstances may not be overly rosey at Wrexham, but at Deepdale, they are at their lowest ebb for many years, as North End already seem doomed for League One football next season.

The Lilywhites have, in recent times, developed a knack for finishing mid-table in the Championship whilst being criticised over a lack of ambition, but that didn't appear to be the case this summer.

Although a Middle-East takeover is yet to be approved, such feats, as well as the club-record signing of Alfie Devine from Tottenham were two key reasons for optimism in Central Lancashire in pre-season.

However, a malaise which saw Preston win just six of their final 23 matches last season following a positive start continued into this campaign, with Paul Heckingbottom replaced by Deepdale cult hero, Graham Alexander, last month.

That said, the Scot is yet to turn the tide and has won just one game out of seven thus far, albeit those three points came before the international break against Southampton.

As such, Rooney's hopes for Wrexham and Preston to reach the Premier League anytime soon are in serious jeopardy, with North End appearing more likely to be overtaken by the third team he wishes extreme luck towards - Stockport County.

The Hatters have, like the Red Dragons, risen from the depths of non-league in recent seasons to have such lofty ambitions under owner, Mark Stott.

Even the exit of current Sheffield Wednesday head coach, Dave Challinor, hasn't derailed County's progress despite suffering play-off agony in the past two seasons, with Jimmy McNulty's side right now second in League One, as only a two-goal swing separates themselves and Huddersfield Town right now.

As such, a return to the Championship for the first time in well over 20 years could restoke a minor rivalry between Stockport and Wrexham from their rise up the pyramid, but it still doesn't change how unlikely Rooney's prediction is to become anytime soon.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Sources indicate that carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville remarked in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United will use the November international break to decide whether Michael Carrick stays on as head coach, after a three-game reprieve that delivered only one win.

According to The Guardian, Carrick came close to being sacked after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada discussed his position at the training ground the following day and agreed to give him three matches to turn things around before the break.

In a recent development, those games brought a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, a 3-2 win over Roma and a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. United conceded eight goals across the three fixtures, and defensive frailty remains the biggest worry.

Sources indicate that wilcox is now leading a review of Carrick’s position. He will consult Berrada before making a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who oversees the club’s sporting operations. Talks are expected to begin on Monday and continue through the break.

The league table makes grim reading. United sit in the Premier League relegation zone with just one league win in their last 10 matches.

If he does win a stay of execution, results will need to follow. Manchester United cannot be languishing in 17th place.

Carrick remains defiant. Speaking to Sky Sports News after the Villa draw, he admitted his side “haven’t won enough games” but insisted he expects to move forward.

“I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games, said Carrick after the late Villa draw.

“I think there’s more than enough [to turn things around].”.

It has been revealed that if United do make a change, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is reported to be Wilcox’s preferred candidate. Howe has been out of work since leaving St James’ Park during pre-season, after four and a half years in charge.

In the meantime, there are no prepares to strengthen Carrick’s coaching staff.

For now, Carrick is expected to be in charge for United’s next match, against Liverpool. Whether three games were enough to convince the hierarchy should become clear before then.

The trip to Anfield could be do or die for the decorated former United midfielder.

He’s not likely to survive a heavy defeat at the home of the club’s fierce rivals, but a galvanising win would surely buy him time and goodwill.

In a recent development, that’s if he makes it through the next fortnight before then. A decision or indication could be two days or two weeks away.

The only certainty at Old Trafford is uncertainty.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ex-Premier League and EFL striker Charlie Austin has branded the decision for Vitor Matos to leave Swansea City for Strasbourg as "strange," but does admit that the French club can be a "stepping stone" to bigger things.

The Portuguese boss's departure hasn't been formally unveiled by Swansea just yet, but Strasbourg themselves revealed that he'd joined their side to replace the outgoing Hugo Oliveira.

In the space of a little under a year, Matos took the South Wales side from 20th in the Championship to a top-half finish last season. Then, he took them to the league's summit during the opening stages of this campaign, before a run of four defeats in five saw them slip down to sixth.

Nevertheless, he had Swansea playing an incredibly attractive, high-intensity brand of football, while also being controlled in possession, too, and it was universally agreed that the Swans had their best chances of promotion in around six years under him.

In a recent development, strasbourg currently sit 13th in Ligue 1 with three wins through their opening 10 games. They aren't in Europe, and some critics would say that the challenge of getting a team like Swansea back into the Premier League would be more satisfying than taking over a struggling team in France.

However, Strasbourg are under the BlueCo banner, the multi-club ownership group which mainly oversees Chelsea, and the French top-flight side is often seen as the little sister, and sometimes even a feeder club, to its Premier League siblings.

Speaking on his "Chaz Kicks Off" YouTube podcast show, former Burnley, QPR and Southampton striker Charlie Austin spoke about how now being under that umbrella could open doors for Matos that Swansea simply couldn't.

"The Swansea manager has departed and gone to Strasbourg, which is strange because they're in a good position," he said.

"But he's obviously been promised the world [by Strasbourg]; it's the stepping stone, isn't it? And we've all seen where it could lead. We saw it with that PE teacher who went to Chelsea, et cetera, so it opens up fresh things.".

While a slightly disrespectful way to refer to him, the "PE teacher" that Austin referenced was Liam Rosenior, who was given the Chelsea job back in January following the departure of Enzo Maresca.

The 42-year-old had spent the previous season and a half at Strasbourg, leading them to a seventh-placed finish in his only full year at the club, and left them in seventh midway through the 2025/26 campaign.

In a recent development, at Chelsea, despite a promising start, seeing only Arsenal beat his side for the first two months of his time at the club, things swiftly unravelled, and he was sacked in late April. He's now back in France, and has Paris FC sitting third in Ligue 1, three points off their neighbours PSG atop the table.

Like Matos, Rosenior was in a Championship job before moving to Strasbourg, and was shortlisted for Manager of the Season in his year at Hull City. The two are following a similar path, and the Portuguese boss may have taken the job with that potentially in mind.

What do you think Vitor Matos' ceiling as a manager is? Let us know in the comments.

Industry observers note that in an ideal world for Chelsea, Xabi Alonso will be a massive success at Stamford Bridge, but if things start to unravel in a year or so, and Matos performs well at Strasbourg, he could be earmarked for that high-profile move. Arguably, as a Jürgen Klopp disciple, he'd have more of a chance than Rosenior did, too.

For Swansea, they now have to make sure that their position in the early-season promotion hunt wasn't down to Matos, and look to maintain the form that got them into the top six in the first place.

The Swans have a few big tests coming up to begin life post-Matos, with West Brom travelling to South Wales on Saturday, followed by a midweek trip to Middlesbrough and then the South Wales derby against Cardiff City a week on Sunday.

This decision from Vitor Matos to leave couldn't have come at a worse time, with not long left of the international break, and Swansea fans will be hoping that the disappointment surrounding it can help bring the squad closer together to pull off some big results.

Hopefully then, by the end of the month, Matos' successor will be in place, and they can help finish the good job that the Portuguese boss has started in the early stages of the campaign.

Gary Neville has launched a furious attack on Manchester United’s leadership over the way the club handled Michael Carrick’s dismissal.

United confirmed on Thursday that Carrick had been sacked, four days after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games.

The club remarked it had reached the “extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary”.

Neville had already branded the process “classless” on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast before the announcement, pointing out that it was widely known Carrick was about to go while United were holding talks with potential replacements.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the decision was confirmed, the former United captain went even further.

“It’s just quite simply disgusting,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that “That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.”.

Neville took particular aim at the decision to hold the crucial meeting in Monaco, with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flying out to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe while Carrick was still taking training at Carrington.

“The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership,” he stated.

It has been revealed that it seems the only ones not to realise that are the trio above, but they aren’t stupid. How they explain it, or attempt to rationalise, it will be painful to listen to.

Neville also argued the club should have acted sooner. Looking back to the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in October, he mentioned United “effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch” as he waved goodbye to supporters at full time, only for the board to hand him three more games.

He summed up the episode as “indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership”.

It’s more than an episode, it’s an omnishambles that reflects the dysfunctional state of MUFC in its current guise.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The passion and intensity of supporters is what makes British football such a good watch, and derby games are particularly special.

There are some fantastic rivalries up and down the divisions, and whilst those in the EFL may not be able to match the media hype that the likes of Arsenal vs Tottenham or Man Utd vs Man City generate, there’s no denying that some of the tastiest derbies in Britain are outside the top flight.

One of those is Blackburn vs Burnley, with the East Lancashire rivals set to meet at Turf Moor on Sunday in what will be a ferocious contest.

With that in mind, FLW has ranked the top EIGHT fiercest rivalries in the Football League….

With Bristol Rovers in League Two, and Bristol City in the Championship, this may be something of a forgotten rivalry, as the two clubs haven’t actually met since 2013.

That was a Johnstone’s Paint Trophy clash, with the Robins coming out on top at Ashton Gate, in what was a brilliant atmosphere. Things did spill over on the night, with home fans invading the pitch, but it also demonstrated how much the game meant.

Unfortunately, we could have to wait some time for the next Bristol derby, but the two clubs not playing for so long will only add to the animosity when they do meet again.

It’s a similar story between Stoke and Port Vale, although you have to go back to 2002 for the last time the two clubs met.

But, the Potters’ U21 side did face Vale in the Checkatrade Trophy back in 2018, with police criticising the ‘despicable’ behaviour of the supporters on the night.

Again, the absence of this fixture on a regular basis will only add to the hatred that develops between the two clubs, and whilst it’s another fixture that may not be played for a long time, it’s still one of the fiercest in the EFL.

The Steel City derby is another fixture that we won’t see this season, but it is a game that has been played regularly over the years, and it’s always a great occasion, whether it’s at Hillsborough or Bramall Lane.

Owls supporters won’t have fond memories of their last encounter, as their relegation was confirmed with a defeat to the Blades, in what was a very tough time for the club.

But, they’re under new ownership now, and they will be determined to get revenge for that when they do meet again, which could be as soon as next season.

Even though Wrexham have forced their way into the conversation about who is the best club in Wales, there’s no denying that the biggest rivalry is between Swansea and Cardiff.

The two clubs have a real hatred for one another, and it’s the first fixture that both sets of supporters look for, and the rivalry resumes at the end of November.

Despite relegation in the 2024/25 campaign, Cardiff hammered Swansea 3-0 in the last meeting, and with both teams doing well in the Championship, it should be a tense occasion.

Next up, we’ve gone for the East Lancashire derby, and neutrals who don’t know what this fixture is all about will get to see it on Sunday.

It’s a fixture that Burnley have ruled in the last decade or so, with Rovers having failed to beat their rivals in 11 attempts, which stretches all the way back to 2010.

But, with the Clarets having not won at home in over a year, and Blackburn in good form, they will believe that Sunday is the perfect opportunity to inflict more pain on Burnley.

The south coast derby is another fierce rivalry in the Championship, and it has already produced drama this season, with Saints beating Pompey on their home patch.

After years apart, the two sides met last season, and whilst the games weren’t the best for neutrals in terms of action, the atmosphere made them a gripping watch.

Portsmouth are having a good season so far, and they will be desperate to get one over their bitter rivals in 2027 when they meet at Fratton Park.

This is another brilliant derby in the Championship right now, with Wolves and West Brom meeting for the first time in front of fans since 2012 earlier this season.

A Fer Lopez goal was enough to give Wolves the bragging rights, with the game played out in front of an electric atmosphere at Molineux.

With Albion and Wolves in the mix for promotion, this rivalry could go up a level throughout the season, and the clash at The Hawthorns later in the season has the potential to be epic.

Will West Brom finish above Wolves this season? Let us know in the comments below.

Finally, the number one rivalry in the EFL has to be West Ham vs Millwall, and the meeting back in September was proof why this rivalry is seen as one of the best in the country.

An exciting game helped, and The Den was rocking when the Lions went two goals up, before West Ham pulled it back to nick a point.

This is another fixture that had been absent for so long, so hatred had been brewing, and most would agree that it is a great addition to the Championship.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have confirmed an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach, with the Argentine set to take charge after the international break.

Industry observers note that the 54-year-old will replace Michael Carrick, who was dismissed on Thursday following United’s disastrous start to the Premier League season. Pochettino is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year contract that will keep him at Old Trafford until the summer of 2029.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is presently managing the United States national team but is expected to fly straight to Manchester after completing his USA international games.

Pochettino will first oversee the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final ties against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday. He is expected to arrive in Manchester on Wednesday before taking charge of the club on Thursday.

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

It has been revealed that pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

It has been revealed that carrick’s departure came less than six months after he signed a two-year contract. His second spell in charge ended after United managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, leaving them in the relegation zone.

Carrick’s coaching staff, including Jonny Evans, Jonathan Woodgate, Steve Holland, Travis Binnion and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson, have all left alongside Carrick.

  • It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

In a recent development, tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

Sources indicate that “I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel remarked. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

Recent findings suggest that “This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

Recent findings suggest that asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

According to recent reports, even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

Industry observers note that “If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel stated. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I remarked, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he stated: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”.

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always mentioned he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”.

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”.

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

It has been revealed that “I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”.

According to recent reports, “It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”.

In a recent development, “The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”.

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a upcoming level of pressure.”.

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

In a recent development, again, not something anyone has remarked to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel: “There was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their (the FA’s) mind.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel states that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sources indicate that sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to states he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”.

Tuchel notes he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”.

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

Sources indicate that “When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel states he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel notes the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel states his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s crucial to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He says the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has noted the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Industry observers note that tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

Ben White pulled out with an injury after being back to his best. It is unfortunately, a bit of a story for him. Josh King was very close and is on the radar.

Industry observers note that tuchel seems to be referring to notes as he speaks. He keeps looking down at a piece of paper he brought in with him.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”.

Recent findings suggest that “They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a fresh competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”.

Industry observers note that we will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

Sources indicate that jason Steele’s inclusion is effectively a call-up. He was at the World Cup as a “fourth” goalkeeper for training – and going to country and western gigs in Kansas – but was not part of the official 26-man squad.
