Published: 12:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:14 EST, 14 November 2026.

In an age where much of the football on show in the English Premier League is so robotic as to be almost unwatchable, flashes of individual brilliance are increasingly becoming things to be cherished.

Across his time at Liverpool and Bournemouth, Ben Gannon-Doak has sporadically distinguished himself as someone who can light up a game by doing something out of the blue and out of the ordinary.

As many a defender will testify, that electric burst of pace across a short distance makes him unplayable at times. He has an X-factor which sets him apart from the crowd.

It has been revealed that what a shame that injuries have restricted his number of appearances to this point. Since moving south from Celtic in 2022, including a loan spell with Middlesbrough, Gannon-Doak has played fewer than 50 times.

At the very time in his career when he could have done with smoothing off the rough edges, he’s spent far too long rehabilitating from one setback or another.

In the build-up to Friday’s match with North Macedonia, Sebastien Pocognoli spoke about how encouraged he was that the player was finally seeing more game time on the south coast, partly as a result of the team’s maiden voyage in Europe.

Ben Gannon-Doak started in a right wing-back role and had an energetic yet frustrating night.

The hope of all concerned was that the recent run of matches which the winger had so evidently needed would translate into a more accomplished display in a Scotland jersey. Alas, this proved to be wishful thinking.

Even against very ordinary opposition, Gannon-Doak’s display proved to be another frustrating watch for the Tartan Army.

Time and time again, he brought them to the edge of their seats by facing up a white jersey and seemingly disappearing in a puff of smoke towards the line. Rarely, however, did the end product materialise.

For a winger with such blinding speed to continually struggle with the all-important final ball is a difficult thing to repeatedly witness.

Recent findings suggest that we shall never know, of course, if the player’s crossing ability would be better by this stage if he hadn’t endured such wretched luck with injuries. But you suspect it’s now just about as good as it’s ever going to be.

The trouble for Pocognoli is that the quality of the delivery from wing-backs into the penalty box is arguably the most notable facet of his preferred 3-4-3 system.

When it breaks down, as it did so often against the group outsiders, the whole thing threatens to grind to a halt.

Gannon-Doak's crossing remains an area of concern for Scotland given his wide position.

Sources indicate that on his record-equalling 102nd cap, Andy Robertson was also guilty of being wasteful on the other flank. Given we know what the skipper has delivered down the years, though, we can write that off as merely a bad night at the office.

The difference with Gannon-Doak is that we’ve rarely seen him tear it up on the flank in a Scotland jersey. So much pace and potential. Not enough positive outcomes when it comes to delivering crosses. In 21 matches, he has three assists and one goal. Those aren’t great numbers.

Just how long do you persevere with a player who doesn’t look to have the requisite skill set for such a specialised and vital position?

Aaron Hickey clearly doesn’t have the pace of the man who he replaced late on, yet he’s hardly a slouch. He is, though, more switched on defensively. And he does know how to cross a football.

It was telling that Gannon-Doak’s most positive contribution of the night against the group outsiders came when he left his station to move infield and take Oli McBurnie’s pass in his stride with the score standing at one-apiece.

In a recent development, his surge towards the goal initially looked like it had been hampered by a heavy touch only for VAR to correctly identify that he’d been impeded by the goalkeeper. He earned his corn in that moment.

John McGinn’s conversion from 12 yards, his second goal of the night, spared Pocognoli’s blushes after a display which didn’t exactly inspire.

That sequence of play certainly raised the possibility that Gannon-Doak could be utilised to better effect in another role.

Gannon-Doak's forward burst led to the award of a penalty and hinted at an alternative role.

If played more centrally, his crossing – undoubtedly his weak spot – would not be such an matter. But the acceleration and driving runs would still be there to cause chaos in and around the penalty box. That will always be his strong suit.

To get the best out of him, maybe the manager needs to redefine him.

Sources indicate that any redeployment would, obviously, create another issue. If Pocognoli remains wedded to the current system, it seems likely that Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson will occupy the two holding berths.

According to recent reports, ahead of them, and behind the main striker, McGinn and Scott McTominay are virtually undroppable. It might be the case then, that Gannon-Doak is eventually utilised as an impact sub. Yet, it would not be a plan without its merits.

Recent findings suggest that he’s got a part to play in this set-up. Probably just not where he’s right now being positioned.

Recent findings suggest that you’d be surprised, frankly, if he started in St Gallen on Monday. Switzerland are a far superior side to North Macedonia, already assured of promotion to League A by topping the section and looking to end this campaign with a flourish against a Scotland side they beat comfortably at Hampden.

According to recent reports, they’ll ask far more questions of Pocognoli’s side. It feels like a task more suited to Hickey.

Scotland, collectively, will need to buck up their ideas if they are to stand any chance of emerging with a positive outcome or, at the least, some credit.

Scotland fans are desperate to see Gannon-Doak succeed but a little change might be needed.

There was a flatness to Friday’s performance, especially in a first half in which the much-vaunted high-press was conspicuous by its absence.

The passing was too safe and predictable. The tempo was low and the play was unimaginative. By half-time, the visitors had fashioned the better chance when Enis Bardhi smashed the ball into the side net.

Scotland were markedly better after the turnaround. After Billy Gilmour’s scarcely believable miss, they were deserving of the opener which came when McGinn burst into the box and lashed home after fine work from Che Adams.

Stemming straight from a corner, North Macedonia’s equaliser – which ended their eight-game goal drought – asked a serious question of Pocognoli’s players.

To their credit, they stepped up with Gannon-Doak’s foray into the box causing the moment of indecision on which the game swung.

The manner of a first Hampden win for Pocognoli won’t live long in the memory. The fervent hope is that it proves to be the start of something.

Leicester City have had a mixed start to the season under Russell Martin, although four wins in their last six League One games suggests they may have turned the corner.

Despite that, Martin still has a lot of work to do to convince the supporters that he is the best long-term solution for the club, and he will know that there’s pressure to take the Foxes back to the Championship at the first attempt.

Whilst there is a lot of quality in the Leicester squad, the opening months of the campaign have proven that further additions are required in January.

However, Leicester’s off-field situation means they won’t be splashing the cash, so the recruitment team will be on the lookout for potential bargains or loan deals to bolster Martin’s ranks.

The fans will have different ideas about where the Foxes need to strengthen, but Leicester aren’t scoring goals at the rate of the best sides in the league, so a latest forward would be welcome.

And, one player who fits the bill is Tawanda Chirewa, with the attacker at the moment on the fringes at Wolves, where he has made eight Championship appearances - all off the bench.

The 23-year-old has failed to truly establish himself at Molineux over the years, and he has had several loan spells in that period.

Raul Jimenez’s injury has given him the opportunity to become a part of Cesar Peixoto’s squad this season, but, when the Mexican returns from injury, along with Bertrand Traore, there is a very real possibility that Chirewa won’t even make the matchday squad.

So, Chirewa will inevitably find himself down the pecking order, but he can obviously change that by taking any more chances that come his way between now and January.

And, to his credit, it should be said that he has made some contributions for Wolves already this season, including scoring a crucial winner at Burnley last month.

Furthermore, Chirewa has been a key player for Zimbabwe, scoring two goals and registering two assists in four group games as The Warriors look to qualify for Africa Cup of Nations.

They still have work to do to get over the line, but Chirewa has been hugely influential in putting his country in a good position with two games to go.

Even though Chirewa could have a role to play, as outlined above, the reality is that he won’t be near the first XI in the long-term, and it would be a shock if that changed.

With that in mind, January feels like it’s the right time for Chirewa to get out and find a permanent home.

Any Leicester fans may be underwhelmed at the prospect of signing Chirewa, as the reality is that loan spells at Derby, Huddersfield and Barnsley haven’t gone to blueprint.

But, Chirewa returned to Wolves with a good attitude in pre-season, where he played well, and he has taken that into the campaign. So, perhaps things have finally come together for the youngster, but he now needs a home to show what he can do on a consistent basis.

Following on from that, Leicester could be a good fit because Chirewa has qualities that Martin will appreciate.

Firstly, he is versatile, which all managers love, as Chirewa could play in any attacking position, whether that’s out wide, as a central striker or in a deeper role.

In a recent development, where do Leicester need to strengthen in January? Let us know in the comments below.

As well as that, he has a good physical profile, and his work-rate and speed make him ideal for pressing from the front - which is what Martin wants from his Leicester side.

Of course, there are areas of Chirewa’s game that he needs to address, and he can get better technically in terms of his ball striking and his finishing, but playing regularly in a Foxes side that look to dominate can help.

So, for what would be a low fee, or even an initial loan, Chirewa could be a potential bargain for Leicester, and he could be a player that Martin moulds into an important figure in their promotion push this season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino officially begins work as United head coach on Wednesday, just four days before his first match against Liverpool at Anfield.

The 54-year-old replaces Michael Carrick, who was dismissed last week after United won just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them 18th in the table.

Pochettino arrives after completing his final assignment with the United States, who beat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

The Argentine has signed a contract until the summer of 2029 and is expected to meet his new players and oversee his first training session on Thursday.

Speaking after his final match with the United States, Pochettino acknowledged the challenge awaiting him in Manchester.

“The new challenge is a major challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel,” he mentioned.

Several members of his coaching staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez, travelled to Manchester earlier this week to begin preparations. Pochettino will have limited time to work with his squad before Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Liverpool, which kicks off at 4.30pm GMT.

The former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager inherits a United side struggling for results after a difficult opening to the campaign. He previously guided Tottenham to the 2019 Champions League final and won the French league title during his spell with Paris Saint-Germain.

According to recent reports, united’s next fixtures also include a Champions League trip to Sporting CP and a home Premier League match against Brentford. Pochettino’s immediate task is to improve United’s league position, beginning with a demanding first match at Anfield.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata has unveiled his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing an end to a beautiful career of around 20 years.

The Spaniard went on to win one of the biggest trophies in professional football. The former Manchester United midfielder confirmed his decision on Wednesday after ending his playing career with Australian side Melbourne Victory.

In a recent development, mata enjoyed a memorable spell at Manchester United after arriving from Chelsea in January 2014. He spent more than eight years at Old Trafford, making 285 appearances, scoring 51 goals and winning four trophies.

His first trophy with Manchester United came in the 2016 FA Cup final against Crystal Palace. He also helped the club win the Community Shield, League Cup and Europa League during the 2016/17 campaign.

According to recent reports, before moving to Manchester, Juan Mata had established himself as one of Chelsea’s most creative players. He won the club’s Player of the Year award in both of his first two full seasons at Stamford Bridge before eventually joining United as David Moyes’ marquee signing.

Sources indicate that mata probably had the biggest moments of his career in the Spain shirt. He earned 41 international caps and scored 10 goals, becoming part of the most talented Spanish team in history. He went on to win the 2010 FIFA World Cup and Euro 2012 with Spain while etching his name in Spanish football history with a goal in Spain’s 4-0 victory over Italy in the European Championship final.

After leaving Manchester United in 2022, the midfielder continued his career with Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before joining Melbourne Victory in September 2025.

His final season in Australia was an impressive one. Mata registered five goals and 13 assists, won the Johnny Warren Medal and earned a place in the A-League Team of the Season.

Reflecting on his decision, Mata spoke about the reason that kept him playing for so many years.

“I was able to keep going for so many years because of the sheer joy of playing,” he remarked.

He also made it clear that retirement would not mean walking away from football altogether.

“Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game.”.

Manchester United also paid tribute to their former midfielder, writing on social media: “Great player, better person. Thank you for representing our colours with class, Juan.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Birmingham City have been issued a warning involving Jay Stansfield ahead of their crucial away trip to Stoke City on Saturday afternoon by modern-day Championship goalscoring supremo, Charlie Austin.

In a recent development, chris Davies' side had won six of their seven games between the final international breaks of 2026, with a 2-1 success against Swansea City at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park on November 7th sending them top ahead of Middlesbrough and the Potters on goal difference.

After finishing 10th in 2025/26, Davies oversaw a relatively quiet summer transfer window in comparison to the two previous years of his tenure, and such a decision has clearly paid off.

The main question concerning Blues right now is whether they have the capability to sustain their promotion challenge for the remaining 31 games, as well as how they seek to add further quality in the January transfer window.

Stansfield's exploits in B9 are often analysed due to the club-record fee Birmingham parted with to sign the forward on a seven-year contract from Fulham in August 2024.

The 23-year-old has received mixed reviews over time, largely down to a decrease in output despite his overall importance within Davies' setup never being questioned.

His brace last time out saw him surpass 50 goals in all competitions for Blues, and is one of several difference-makers on show in Saturday's game at the Bet365 Stadium.

Discussing the clash with Stoke, Austin said: "The clubs that have been in those positions are wanting to get back. It's nice to see the usual names up there and performing.

In a recent development, "We're having this conversation in November. The way the Championship is, give it the week before Christmas and you could be at the opposite end.

According to recent reports, "It's going to be a fascinating game," the former striker claimed. "The thing is with Birmingham, for me, they heavily rely on Jay Stansfield.

It has been revealed that "That's my only concern with Birmingham. If anything happens to him, they're in big trouble.".

Stansfield has been viewed as the figurehead of Knighthead's ambitious project at Birmingham, but many supporters are likely to disagree with Austin's claim on the England youth international.

In the past three seasons, the striker may have hit double-figures, emphasising his importance whilst also adjusting to his current 'number 10' role, but there certainly doesn't appear to be an over-reliance on his services anymore.

Birmingham have scored three or more goals in four of their last six encounters, with the goals very much shared around during that timeframe as the likes of Alex Cochrane, Max Bird, Liam Millar, Demarai Gray and August Priske have all netted as well as Stansfield.

Davies will be pleased with how well the attacker has led the line in the victories over Millwall and Swansea in Priske's absence, which, in itself, creates a selection headache ahead of the matchup with Mark Robins' side.

With Stoke and Birmingham level on points, even with 30 matches to play afterwards, the potential victors in North Staffordshire have the chance to use the game as a springboard for future success.

The Potters have only lost once since August, which came in a narrow 3-2 defeat to Middlesbrough on October 13th, although both of Blues' two defeats came on the road against Norwich City and Cardiff City.

It has been revealed that as Austin alluded to, a fascinating contest lies in wait with both squads strong in defence and possessing attacking flair. Davies will be hoping Stansfield continues his impressive form whatever role he is assigned, whilst also needing his 10 teammates to step up to the plate as they have so often done.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'.
  • It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026.

Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'.

It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field,' Pochettino said when his contract was signed.

Yet, after a few months and one international window, that experiment to make a 'lasting impact' has ended. Pochettino may have cried because he fell in love with the country, but it's not like he got fired. Instead, he's off to lead one of the world's greatest football brands in Manchester United.

According to recent reports, so now the question turns to the legacy Pochettino leaves behind. Plenty of American soccer writers and fans point to the spirit the former Chelsea boss created and how he helped to energize a team which had been bogged down by past coaches.

Sources indicate that but Pochettino's results don't scream success. The World Cup finish was nothing special compared to his peers, his record against the best nations the USA faced was poor and he'll leave as the first full-time USMNT manager in nearly 30 years to not win at least one trophy.

Mauricio Pochettino cried as he left the United States' top job for Manchester United.

Pochettino's USMNT played exciting football, but ultimately didn't progress past the norm.

But any potential for further growth evaporated when the Argentine returned to England.

By all accounts, the greatest thing Pochettino did was install a hungry, all-in-or-nothing culture in a team bogged down by an earth-rocking scandal and a poor 2024 Copa America run.

Industry observers note that but he did so in a way that often left the biggest players of the USMNT system behind. Rather than keep a consistent core of his best players around, he seemed intent on tinkering with the lineup in each window.

According to recent reports, the results reflect that instability. Leading to the World Cup, Pochettino played 12 games against sides in the top 30 of the FIFA World Rankings. He won just three fixtures – drawing once and losing the remaining eight.

All the while, he was linked to returns to Europe. Pochettino may have mentioned in his exit press conference that he 'never said I wanted to go back to the Premier League' but the Premier League certainly wanted him – especially Tottenham.

Come World Cup time, Pochettino's team finally seemed to gel with a scintillating style of play never before seen in the USMNT.

It has been revealed that but it all crashed down after the Round of 32 game against Bosnia when Folarin Balogun's red card was (as this American will admit) deviously overturned. The noise and controversy led to the Americans' embarrassment at the hands of Belgium on home soil.

A summer of exciting soccer for the USMNT followed years of hard resets and mixed results.

It all fell apart with a demolition by Belgium, leaving Pochettino without any success.

Recent findings suggest that the Yanks were not expected to go much further than the last 16. But branding Pochettino's time atop the USMNT a 'success' on the back of this World Cup performance is giving him too much credit – especially considering the four prior managers to take the US to the World Cup all made it to that stage of the tournament as well.

With his departure confirmed, Pochettino is the first USMNT manager to leave the post without any silverware since the 1998 departure of Steve Sampson, who hadn't been a professional manager before being appointed to the job.

Even though he achieved little in terms of results, players praised Pochettino's leadership and development skills, which shouldn't be ignored.

Industry observers note that middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said: 'He's meant so much to me and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you.'.

Industry observers note that but not every player in the system was tripping over themselves to play under Poch. Just ask Christian Pulisic, who took the entire summer off in 2025 to rest before the World Cup – only to put up a goose egg in his home country.

Any hope for further progress under Pochettino evaporated when United came calling.

All of this being said, there was reason for hope in the future. By re-signing Pochettino, the chance to cement that work ethic, culture and leadership presented itself.

With his extension, Pochettino had the chance to build a foundation in US Soccer to engender future success for decades to come.

Now, that's all gone. Now, Pochettino's time in charge will be remembered more for unfulfilled potential than culture shifting. After all, how do you expect to keep a culture if its chief architect leaves?

US Soccer now is faced with a quagmire of either hiring the biggest possible name again (Guardiola, if you believe the rumors) or hiring someone who will treat the position less like a stepping stone and more like a cornerstone.

Industry observers note that it never seemed like Pochettino fully embraced the US, despite the tears on Friday. He'll be off for Old Trafford and a United squad bogged down by perpetual disappointment, all while leaving behind the biggest "What If" in the still-growing history of the American game.

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:39.

Appearing in the MLS Cup playoffs for the first time since 2023, the New England Revolution will welcome the Philadelphia Union to Gillette Stadium for game one of that best-of-three series on Saturday.

The Revs finished the regular season as the third seed in the Eastern Conference, losing 1-0 to Orlando City on Decision Day, while the Union wound up in sixth, defeating Toronto 4-1 in their final match before the playoffs.

It has been quite the first year for Marko Mitrovic in New England as the Serbian helped the club improve by 22 points from the 2025 regular season.

They earned twice as many victories in 2026 when compared to 2025, including seven more on home soil.

That said, they enter the post-season on a bit of a downward spiral, losing their last two league fixtures and scoring just one goal over that stretch.

At the same time, the club will try to end a four-match losing run in the post-season Saturday and win their first MLS Cup playoff encounter at Foxborough since the 2020 Play-in Round, when they beat Montreal 2-1.

Among all the 2026 Eastern Conference playoff teams, the Revolution were one the best defensively, conceding the second fewest goals (47).

On Saturday, they can extend their winning run versus Philly to three matches, having triumphed in both league games against them this year, including a come-from-behind 2-1 victory at Gillette Stadium in May.

Fresh England were not the only team with a great comeback story in 2026, as the Union transformed dramatically after an early-season slump.

Ryan Richter turned this team around, losing just two matches since taking charge in late May, after Philly had won just one of their first 15 league fixtures of the year.

Down the stretch of the campaign, however, the club regressed a little, dropping points in four of their last five regular season encounters.

This weekend they can snap a two-match winless run away from home versus MLS opposition, collecting six domestic victories in 2026, two fewer than the year before.

The Union have won two of their last three MLS playoff games as the visitors, including a 3-0 win at the Chicago Fire in 2025.

Philly have won three of their last four meetings with the Revs domestically and eliminated them from the 2023 post-season, winning that best-of-three first round series 2-0.

  • Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Sources indicate that pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the fresh manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha said, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

Industry observers note that “Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”.

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one big problem for Pochettino.

Rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United. Highlighting a major problem, Smith remarked, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Queens Park Rangers are well-positioned for a push towards a play-off place following a decent start to the season, but one of their players hasn't been getting a look in.

It has been revealed that as teams return from the last international break of 2026, Queens Park Rangers are in a fairly strong position in the EFL Championship. Rangers return in 8th place in the table, and with the division's play-off places having been expanded from four to six from this season, staying there would be enough to earn them a shot at a place in the Premier League should they be able to maintain their position.

But success for a club doesn't necessarily mean success for all of their players, and for their Trinidad & Tobagan international forward Justin Obikwu, opportunities have been thin on the ground. Having made only a handful of appearances for the club since his £500,000 move from Coventry City in January 2026, Obikwu will be crying out for some game-time, and the January transfer window could give him the opportunity to get some of that in by going elsewhere for the remainder of this season.

In a recent development, while Queens Park Rangers have been going reasonably well so far throughout 2026-27, things have been more difficult for forward Justin Obikwu. The forward had started last season on loan at Lincoln City, but was recalled by Coventry in January to be sold to Rangers.

The move to QPR has not brought him many more opportunities than he was getting in the West Midlands, though.

He didn't make a single appearance for Rangers throughout the second half of last season, and this season has brought only three appearances from the bench and a total of 34 minutes on the pitch, while the attacking positions have been occupied by a combination of Richard Kone, Paul Smith, Koki Saito, Alfie Lloyd, Kwame Poku and Rumarn Burrell.

It has been revealed that do you think Justin Obikwu should get more game-time at QPR this season? Let us know in the comments below!

Obikwu finally made his debut for QPR from the bench against Cardiff City at the start of September, and has followed that up with brief appearances in their last two matches before the last international break, against Burnley and Lincoln. These appearances may give the forward hope that he'll get further opportunities before the end of this year, but there's no guarantee of this and if it doesn't happen for him before January, it might turn out more prudent for him to go elsewhere and get that all-important game-time.

Justin Obikwu was spotted in the youth system at non-league Harefield United and signed by Coventry City in 2021, signing his first senior professional contract two years later, but he never got to make a single appearance for the Midlands club. Instead, over the two and a half years that he was on the books with Coventry, he was sent out on loan on three occasions, twice to Grimsby Town and then to Lincoln City.

His second spell at Grimsby offered a glimpse of his potential. Although not a regular in the first team at Blundell Park, he still managed seven goals in 19 League appearances for Grimsby, and his loan move to Lincoln City for 2025-26 was a clear step up for him.

It has been revealed that but since arriving at Loftus Road in January, he hasn't been picked in a QPR starting eleven yet. He made one appearance for their youth team in a 4-1 Premier League Cup win against Bolton Wanderers in the middle of August, in which he scored, but his appearances from the bench for the first team since then have been both brief and sporadic.

Appearing from the bench in the last two consecutive matches prior to the international break offers him a glimmer of light, but there are no guarantees that he'll get more game-time and, if anything, Queens Park Rangers are slightly overstocked with young attacking players at the moment.

Recent findings suggest that A move to a League One or League Two club in the January transfer window, then, would make sense. Such a move doesn't have to close the door on him having a future at Loftus Road. He may even impress enough to enhance his chances of pushing for a first-team place for the 2027-28 season. And the club would get the opportunity to see what he can do without regular game-time without having to take any risks themselves.

Now 22 years of age, Justin Obikwu's career could be approaching a crossroads. He still has the potential to shine in the higher divisions of the EFL, but his progress has stalled, and after almost a year with Queens Park Rangers, his opportunities have remained limited. Some time away from Loftus Road could reignite his career and give his club the opportunity to see whether he can develop further as a player.

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:47.

The Western Conference playoffs begin on Saturday when Dallas take on the Portland Timbers in game one of that best-of-three series at Toyota Stadium in Frisco.

Los Toros finished the MLS regular season in second place in the West, defeating the Colorado Rapids 3-1 in their last outing, while Portland wound up in seventh thanks to a 2-0 win at Austin FC.

Consistency was the name of the game for Dallas throughout the 2026 campaign, as they had their highest regular season finish in the West since 2016 (first).

In 2026, Eric Quill’s men did not lose more than two consecutive league fixtures and have not suffered successive defeats domestically since April.

They won the joint-third-most games in the Western Conference this season at home (nine), and have not lost a home playoff game this decade.

During the 2026 regular season, they averaged the second-most goals per game (1.8) among Western Conference sides, netting three or more at home on seven separate occasions.

Expectations were relatively low for this team heading into the season, but given where they finished, there is a belief that this might be the year they claim that elusive first MLS Cup.

Dallas are unbeaten in their last six MLS meetings versus the Timbers, and have not lost any of their last six home games against them.

Down the stretch of the campaign with their playoff lives hanging in the balance, Portland stepped up in a major way.

Marti Cifuentes saw his side win their last four matches of the regular season and go unbeaten in their last five games to secure a place in the opening round.

The Timbers have never won their opening playoff encounter in a best-of-three series, losing 2-1 at San Diego in their opener last year.

Portland won their final two MLS away games of 2026 and, on Saturday, can claim their first road playoff win since 2021 at the Colorado Rapids (1-0).

In 2026, they missed the fourth-most big chances in the Western Conference while creating the third-most in their conference.

Saturday will mark the third time they face Los Toros away from home in the post-season, and the Timbers have yet to lose in Frisco come playoff time.

Dallas Major League Soccer form:.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:.

There is only one notable injury to report for Dallas heading into this weekend with Geovane Jesus out due to a cruciate ligament tear.

Joaquin Valiente, Kaick and Santiago Moreno all found the back of the net for them on Decision Day after the Rapids took the lead early in the second half.

On the Portland side, Juan David Mosquera is dealing with a foot and ankle problem, Zac McGraw has a sore back, Brandon Bye is questionable with a knee injury and Alex Bonetig is doubtful because of a shoulder strain.

Ariel Lassiter and Kristoffer Velde netted in their victory over Austin, while James Pantemis collected the clean sheet with seven stops.

Dallas possible starting lineup:.

Daniel; Johansson, Ibeagha, Urhoghide, Moore; Valiente, Ramiro, Kaick, Kamungo; Farrington, Musa.

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:.

Pantemis; Hernandez, Surman, Waterman, Smith; Da Costa, Caicedo, Izoita; Velde, Janssen, Lassiter.

All season long, Dallas have been potent in the attacking third at home, and against an inconsistent defensive unit like the Timbers, we believe Los Toros will create enough scoring opportunities to win.

For now, Paz remains a reported target rather than a player involved in active transfer talks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Malo Gusto’s World Cup has suddenly become more than a France subplot for Chelsea. It is now a live assessment of whether Xabi Alonso inherits a right-back worth protecting, reshaping or trading at the peak of his market.

Chelsea’s own interview with Gusto this week underlined the human part of that equation. The 23-year-old spoke about learning from N’Golo Kante, calling the former Blue one of the best midfielders France have produced and stressing the value of his example on and off the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that that matters because Kante is not just a nostalgic reference point. He remains the standard Chelsea supporters still use when judging humility, intensity and reliability in a high-pressure dressing room.

For Gusto, those qualities arrive at a decisive moment. Reports around the player’s future claim Chelsea value him at around £75million, with the imminent Marco Palestra deal creating a more crowded full-back picture.

That number looks aggressive, but the logic is clear. Gusto is young, capped by France, under contract, Premier League-tested and capable of playing in several defensive structures.

🚨🚨| NEW: Chelsea are open to selling Malo Gusto this summer, with his agent already in 𝐓𝐀𝐋𝐊𝐒 with Manchester City and Inter. Chelsea will only sell if their valuation is met.{@siphillipssport} pic.twitter.com/vNR2bWud9F.

The easiest reading of Gusto’s Kante comments is sentimental. It should not be.

For Alonso, who officially begins work on July 1, the vital detail is what those comments say about the player Chelsea have been developing.

Gusto has not always looked completely settled at Stamford Bridge. His best games have carried thrust, speed and recovery power, while his less convincing spells have raised questions about final-ball quality and defensive concentration.

That uncertainty is exactly why the next coach matters.

Alonso’s previous teams have leaned heavily on wide players who can receive under pressure, attack space early and still protect the back line when possession breaks down. Gusto has the athletic base for that job.

The test is whether his decision-making can be refined enough to make him a structural piece rather than a rotation asset.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the more surprising standout players in the Championship this season has been Cardiff City's Jack Moylan.

In a recent development, no player in the EFL has had a better 2026 than the Irishman. At Lincoln City, he missed the opening stages of last season due to an ankle injury, but even before then, he was a sporadic player for Michael Skubala's side, scoring nine in 54 in all competitions in the year-and-a-half he'd spent at Sincil Bank.

Since the turn of the year, though, he dominated in League One for the Imps en route to the third-tier title, scoring 10 and assisting five in 20 outings between January 17th and the end of the season.

He debuted over the summer and has since become a regular for the Republic of Ireland National team and now has 10 goals in 15 Championship outings for Cardiff City.

It's been an exceptional year for Moylan, and one that's making those at Sheffield United and Derby County feel a little jealous.

Moylan developed late in life. It took him until 25 years old to emerge as a top talent in the Championship, but even in his teenage years, the Irishman wasn't as developed physically as others his age.

In an interview with the Irish Independent in the wake of yet another call-up to the Republic of Ireland national team earlier this month, the Cardiff attacker spoke about how Irish legend Damien Duff convinced him to join Shelbourne in 2022 after leaving Bohemians, and how he helped him get in shape to tackle the EFL.

Moylan said that Duff bluntly telling him to "get in better shape" brought him back to teenage rejection. At 16, Sheffield United, Derby and then-Premier League side Watford all took a look at him, but declined to sign him as he was "too small" and "not developed enough.".

The 25-year-old grew up to the reported six-foot-one he is now in his later teenage years, and Duff was the manager who helped him build strength alongside that growth.

Damien Duff had a brilliant managerial career at Shelbourne, with the highlight being winning the Premier Division title back in 2024, ending an 18-year drought.

But he also helped develop talent who have gone on to sign for EFL clubs. The likes of Harry Wood, who is now lighting up League One with Stockport County and Lewis Temple, who Bolton Wanderers signed back in January, all played under Duff at Shelbourne.

Moylan is the pick of the bunch, though, who got his EFL move off the back of a 15-goal campaign in the 2023 LOI Premier Division campaign.

It was there that the Irishman started to carve out the role he would go on to play both at Lincoln and now at Cardiff, an unnatural number 10 who basically operates as a second striker behind a main line-leader and who can deputise as the nine if needed.

In the end, Moylan's rejection allowed him to carve out this career under Duff, and then prove himself in the Championship at a later date.

Moylan hit headlines at Lincoln; so much so that Cardiff, a side that only made four newly introduced signings in the summer, made him their marquee arrival.

He cost £3 million, and while Bluebirds fans knew how dangerous he was in the division below at Sincil Bank, the attacking midfielder had never played at Championship level. It was a slight risk, but one which has paid off massively.

It has been revealed that moylan has maintained his quality from that attacking-midfield / striker role. He's not afraid to take shots, despite the step-up and the move to a new team — he has the most in the division — and they're high-quality chances, too, with only teammate Yousef Salech and the Championship's top scorer Will Lankshear having a higher personal xG.

How many goals do you think Jack Moylan will score this season? Let us know in the comments.

That first-half hat-trick against West Ham United in the penultimate game before the international break ensured that his performances were hitting the mainstream in the second-tier, too.

Industry observers note that numbers like these won't go unnoticed, and it won't be long before Premier League and other top-flight sides are poking their heads round Cardiff's door and enquiring about how much it'd cost for them to part ways. I can guarantee it'll be a lot more than the £3m they spent to bring him in.

Ultimately, with how young players break into first-team squads these days, signing a 16-year-old who wasn't developed physically and deemed too short to make it at a top level would have been seen as a questionable one.

Hindsight is a wonderful thing, though, and those who were sent to scout Moylan from the likes of Sheffield United, Derby and Watford must be feeling pretty frustrated that the Irishman slipped through their fingers.

In a recent development, granted, perhaps working under Damien Duff was exactly the catalyst the 25-year-old needed to reach this stage. At any of those three English sides, he may not have been given the required support. Either way, Cardiff have been the benefactors of that decision right now.

According to recent reports, the Bluebirds are playing some incredibly attractive, attacking football, and their record at home is exceptional. If they tidy things up both defensively and on the road, they could be a side primed for a late top-eight push.

Moylan will need to keep firing to ensure that happens, and if he can reach 20 goals this season, he'll go down as one of the best signings in the Championship this season, and perhaps in Cardiff's history.

Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and stated recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Rice is aware of what Souness has mentioned but believes his return of 22 goals and 33 assists since joining the Gunners in 2023 disproves the former Liverpool midfielder's opinion.

In a recent development, ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,’ mentioned Rice. ‘For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’.

According to recent reports, rice, who will start as an advanced midfielder when England take on Spain here in Madrid on Sunday night, added: ‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’.

Rice also believes Souness, 73, may not understand how the game has evolved.

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has laughed off Graeme Souness' criticism after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Pundit Souness believes Rice would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Sources indicate that ‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man's football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ began Rice. 'We played him the other week and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball. The game is different now. It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It's changed a lot, and you're always trying to look for tactical advantages.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I'm constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He's constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we're now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There's no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he's done.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I didn't get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I've never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’.

Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

📅 19 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4634 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents.
  • In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns.
  • Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

In a recent development, remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Sources indicate that not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

In a recent development, gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Industry observers note that arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

In a recent development, it was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it rapidly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

According to recent reports, both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another latest signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

It has been revealed that “The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 01:53.

Inter Miami begin their MLS Cup title defence on Saturday when they host the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in game one of that best-of-three series.

The defending champions finished second in the Eastern Conference by two points, drawing their final regular-season outing at home to Charlotte FC, 3-3, while the Crew snuck in as the seventh seed with a thrilling 4-3 win over the Chicago Fire.

Miami will hope to take the first step toward more history on Saturday as they aim to become the first Eastern Conference club this century to capture consecutive MLS Cups.

If they can pull it off, they would be the first MLS side to do so since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2011 and 2012 and the second ever to achieve that feat in the East, after DC United..

Kily Gonzalez has seen his team drop points in three of their last four league encounters, though they have only suffered one defeat since October.

Thanks in large part to captain Lionel Messi, Miami led the regular season in goals with 80, one fewer than they managed a year ago.

The Herons also led the league in goals per match (2.4) and have netted three or more times in four of their last five post-season outings.

Saturday will mark the first time they meet Columbus in the playoffs, and Inter Miami having never lost a home game against the Crew.

A team that could barely buy a win at the start of the regular season could seemingly do no wrong down the stretch of it.

The Crew began 2026 without a win in their first five league games but will enter the playoffs as one of the hottest teams remaining, riding a six-match winning streak.

Laurent Courtois has unlocked this team’s scoring potential, with Columbus netting multiple times in nine straight MLS affairs, with three or more goals in four of those instances.

This weekend they can end a three-match playoff losing run away from home, having won just one post-season affair since lifting the MLS Cup in 2023.

As potent as they have been in front of goal lately, this side have rarely shown much defensive poise away from home, conceding three or more goals in seven MLS games this year outside of ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Columbus won their only previous playoff game in the Sunshine State, defeating Orlando City 2-0 in 2023 en route to winning the MLS Cup later that year.

A shoulder issue will likely keep Mateo Silvetti on the Miami sidelines on Saturday, while Tadeo Allende is dealing with a knee problem, Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear and Cesar Abadia is doubtful due to a groin strain.

Messi finished the regular season as the top goalscorer for a second year running, though it was Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul who netted for them on Decision Day.

There is one injury concern on the Columbus side heading into this encounter as Wessam Abou Ali is doubtful because of a knee injury.

Gonzalo Tapia notched a brace for the Crew against the Fire, with Anass Zaroury and Brais Mendez also scoring, with the latter netting the winner in stoppage time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa academy graduate TJ Carroll is attracting loan interest from clubs in the EFL, with it expected that the youngster sources regular first-team football away from Villa Park in January.

That is according to the Daily Mail's Midlands football correspondent, Tom Collomosse, with the Championship pair of Portsmouth and Swansea City namedropped, as well as League One strugglers, Barnsley.

Villa are currently in the midst of another campaign involving European football under Unai Emery, with the Spaniard bringing home a first trophy in 30 years five months ago in the form of the UEFA Europa League.

The B6 club have given plenty of exposure to young talents throughout Emery's four-year tenure, and Carroll is one of many who have earned praise for their performance levels in the club's highly-successful youth setup.

The Villans have already sanctioned two loans involving Championship sides this campaign, with Joe Gauci and Samuel Iling-Junior joining Lincoln City and Bolton Wanderers respectively, and a third could be in store involving Carroll.

The centre-back has progressed through the Bodymoor Heath ranks from Under-9s level to now being on the fringes of Emery's new-look first-team.

It is now claimed that such progress has alerted Portsmouth, Swansea and Barnsley, with the South Coast side already agreeing three Premier League loans so far including Brentford's Benjamin Arthur, although the centre-back is currently sidelined with a stress fracture.

The Tykes have also aided the progress of the aforementioned Gauci in recent times, as the Australian goalkeeper was loaned to the South Yorkshire club in 2024/25, and they would hope for a repeat involving Carroll.

Carroll's first-team exposure with Villa mainly came in pre-season ahead of the current campaign, which included outings against League Two promotion hopefuls Walsall, as well as FC Porto, Real Sociedad and BG Pathum United.

The youngster, who has 30 appearances at Under-21s level under his belt, has also featured in the UEFA Youth League, with Villa qualifying for the tournament through the exploits of Emery's first-team last term, and recently scored twice against FC Barcelona in a 3-3 draw.

Collomosse's report states that Pompey, the Swans and Tykes do face competition for Carroll's services in the form of Norwegian outfit, Viking FK.

The Stavanger-based outfit have gained notoriety in recent months for their own Champions League qualification, which includes a 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich, although their trip to Villa Park last month ended in a 3-1 loss.

With there being over a month until the January transfer window opens, circumstances may change which determine Carroll's potential destination, albeit one major call could have already influenced such decisions.

Swansea have conceded just 18 times in their first 15 Championship fixtures, but a poor run of recent results has now been compounded by Vitor Matos' controversial move to Ligue 1 side, RC Strasbourg.

In a recent development, the point is not simply that Chelsea once had Olise in the building. It is that his rise provides a hard benchmark for the type of final-third specialist Xabi Alonso must either develop or buy.

Chelsea have spent heavily on attacking upside. Olise’s rise is a reminder that the real separator is not potential, but repeatable elite production.

Bayern’s own season review underlines why the conversation has accelerated.

The German champions confirmed Olise finished 2025/26 with 25 goals and 28 assists from 57 competitive appearances. He was also named Bayern’s Player of the Season for a second straight year, finishing ahead of Harry Kane and Luis Diaz in the fan vote.

That is elite production from a wide creator who does not play like a chalk-on-boots winger.

Olise can receive wide, drift inside, manipulate the half-space and still deliver the last pass at match-winning speed. Chelsea have bought attackers with pieces of that profile, but few have joined the dots with that level of consistency.

There is an obvious recruitment lesson here.

The market will now price that blend of creativity, ball security and goal threat close to superstar territory. If Chelsea want an Alonso attack that controls games rather than simply runs through them, the next winger decision cannot be judged on pace or upside alone.

It has to be judged on game control, final-third calm and repeat output.

Bundesliga’s tournament analysis was even more revealing. It noted that Olise had reached 10 France goal involvements in 18 appearances and was named Player of the Match on his World Cup debut against Senegal.

That same analysis highlighted the tactical adjustment that moved Olise closer to Kylian Mbappe after half-time. His passing range then became the lever that changed the game.

According to recent reports, that matters for Chelsea because Alonso’s best Bayer Leverkusen sides were built around players who could receive between lines without killing the tempo. Cole Palmer already gives Chelsea one version of that.

The wider question is whether the squad has another attacker who can bend matches from the opposite side without turning every possession into a one-v-one.

According to recent reports, olise’s Chelsea connection can easily become sentimental. The sharper editorial point is structural.

This is the calibre of player who once passed through the academy pathway and later became a global-level attacker elsewhere. Chelsea cannot change that history, but they can use it to stress-test the next wave of decisions.

That matters for Tyrique George, Kendry Paez, Estevao and any latest wide signing.

ReadChelsea has already looked at how Tyrique George’s likely Everton return gives Alonso a fresh winger audit. Olise’s current standing raises the standard of that discussion.

Recent findings suggest that he is no longer just a former academy name or a missed Premier League target. He is evidence of what happens when technical security, role clarity and patience meet elite coaching.

For Alonso, that is the real value of the Olise noise.

It has been revealed that chelsea do not need to turn every academy exit into regret. They do need to recognise the standard now being set by one of Cobham’s former pupils.

The next wide forward who gets serious minutes at Stamford Bridge has to be assessed against that ceiling, not against the safer language of potential.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

Recent findings suggest that reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

According to recent reports, according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

In a recent development, “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

That statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Industry observers note that prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a big boost. It could help fund fresh signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

The Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

According to recent reports, “Before the match against Fiorentina (on 24 August), I remarked it would be difficult for us to deprive ourselves of notable players so near to the end of the transfer session, and so it proved. Kone is an important player, we’re happy he stayed with us, and we’re confident he’ll give his contribution during the season.”.

Chelsea’s midfield has changed shape under Xabi Alonso since the summer, with Morgan Rogers arriving to add depth and competition for places. That signing came during a window that also saw exits acceleration under Xabi Alonso, as the head coach reshaped his squad around his own style.

It has been revealed that koné’s ball winning and his range of progressive passing would suit Alonso well, should Chelsea ever revisit their interest. Supporters have already seen how Alonso rotates his midfield for the biggest games, including the recent derby line-up selections against Brentford.

It has been revealed that for now, Rogers and Chelsea’s existing central options give Alonso enough cover without needing an immediate signing. Roma’s reluctance to sell also means any deal would need patience rather than a quick resolution.

In a recent development, nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'.

Owono stated he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono).

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono.

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

Diogo Dalot has become one of the targets of Manchester United supporters’ dissatisfaction, but Gary Neville believes the Portuguese full-back is far from being one of the squad’s main problems.

The former Manchester United captain came out in defence of his fellow right-back after the boos Dalot received at Old Trafford and said he would get rid of other players before parting with the number two.

The criticism comes at a time of instability for Manchester United, who are struggling to find consistency in the Premier League and are again facing questions over the individual performances of their players. Dalot was one of the negative protagonists in the draw with Aston Villa, particularly because of the penalty he conceded, and his substitution during the game was greeted with celebrations by the home fans.

It has been revealed that ‘I would be getting rid of some players before Dalot. Dalot got booed last week at Old Trafford and I was really surprised at that’ - the former full-back mentioned on the ‘Stick to Football’ podcast.

In Neville’s view, Dalot is receiving excessive criticism for frequently playing out of his natural position. The Portuguese is a right-back, but has also been used on the left side, either as a full-back or wing-back, depending on the team’s needs.

The former Manchester United player stressed that this change of role requires adaptation and that Dalot indicates a positive attitude in accepting the tasks given to him by the manager.

‘If you put me at left wing-back or left-back, and I am a right-back, and he is too, I would say: “No way, why are you putting me there?”’.

The pundit, however, believes Dalot has shown a willingness to help the team, even when he has to play in a position different from the one in which he feels most comfortable.

‘Instead, Dalot literally sticks his hand up and says: “Go on, I’ll play there, I will do anything for the team”. I never see him shirk anything, I never look at him and think he could try harder’ - he added.

It has been revealed that neville’s defence does not mean the full-back is free from criticism of his performances. The Portuguese struggled against Aston Villa and conceded a penalty that contributed to the result. The former captain, however, believes individual performance needs to be analysed within the context of a squad with collective problems and players often shifted out of their usual roles.

According to recent reports, neville also compared Dalot with other members of Manchester United’s defensive unit and stated there are players who should be sold before the Portuguese. The former full-back specifically named Noussair Mazraoui, Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt.

‘I watch defenders very closely and, if you ask me, I would be getting rid of Mazraoui, well gone, before him, I would be getting rid of Martinez well before him, I would be getting rid of De Ligt gone before him.’.

It has been revealed that the opinion stands out because the three players named have also faced questions at different points of the season. Mazraoui has been used in different defensive roles, while Martinez has dealt with injury problems and controversy. De Ligt, meanwhile, has also been subject to the team’s fluctuations in performance and changes to the defensive set-up.

It has been revealed that dalot joined Manchester United in 2018 from Porto and has had different spells at the club. After a loan at Milan, he returned to Old Trafford and earned a place in the team, particularly during the 2022-23 season. Since then, he has become a regular presence, although his use on both sides of defence has fuelled debate about his best position.

In a recent development, while the club try to find stability, the Portuguese remains a recurring option in defence. For Neville, the pressure on the full-back should not be greater than that directed at other players who, in his assessment, have performed worse or contributed less to the team’s needs.
